and that there should be in it a prefect (shiḥna) from the territory of Sanjar.
The Caliph, however, replied:
"We have no authority over Sanjar,
nor do we accept a prefect of his.
And if Zengi desires peace from us,
let him deliver Dubays to us,
and he may sit in peace in Mosul.
And if not,
behold, we are marching against him."
And in the first month of the year 527,
the Caliph and his son [proclaimed]:
Sanjar,
then Mas'ud,
then David his brother,
all three of them together as Sultans.
And the Caliph al-Mustarshid marched against Mosul,
and besieged it for eighty days,
but was not able to conquer it.
And when news reached him
that Sultan Mas'ud had rebelled against him,
he abandoned Mosul and returned to Baghdad.
And Joscelin the Second took the fortress in Shabakhtan (or Shabashtan),
and demolished it completely.
And John, the king of the Greeks, set out and took the fortress of Kastamonu peacefully from the Turks.
And he also took two other fortresses in battle,
and destroyed them.
And Baldwin, the Frankish king of Jerusalem, took by battle the fortress of al-Qusayr, which is near Antioch,
and went out (or they went out) to 'Amq.
And there the Turks gathered against the Franks like locusts.
And at first the Franks fled before the Turks until they drew them into the plain.
Then they dismounted and sought pardon from one another,
and turned back against the Turks,
and dealt them a great blow until evening.
These things happened in the year 1445 [of the Greeks].

And the Christians took refuge in the chosen one, Mor Bar Sauma,
and they sent and brought the reliquary (glosqoma) in which was the right hand of the saint.
And as soon as it arrived,
a miracle occurred,
and the locusts departed,
without having damaged anything at all in the entire country.
The Greeks, however, burning with envy,
incited the Latin (Frankish) Metropolitan Papias to open the reliquary,
so that the right hand might be revealed.
And when the monks were unwilling,
the Greeks mocked [saying: "Bar] Sauma is not a saint,
but as a heretic he was condemned by the Ecumenical Synod that [at..."].
